transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Name]. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Um… I guess I’m here because I’ve just felt really low for a long time. Like, the last couple years, it’s this heavy, empty feeling that doesn’t really go away, even when I’m at work or church or with people I care about.
Have you noticed that you don’t enjoy things anymore, even activities that used to make you happy, like hobbies, time with friends, or going to church?
I don’t know… I haven’t really thought about it that way. I still do some things, but I’m not sure if I’d say I enjoy them much.
Would you say that you no longer take pleasure in things you used to enjoy, or that you’ve lost interest in them?
I’m… not really sure. I still show up to things, so it’s hard to tell. I guess it doesn’t feel the same, but I don’t know if I’d call it losing interest.
Can you think back to things you used to enjoy, like hobbies or spending time with loved ones—do you still find pleasure in those activities, or do they feel different now?
I mean… they do feel different, I guess. I still do them sometimes, but it’s not like I really feel much from it. It’s hard to explain.
So, just to be clear, would you say that you no longer take pleasure in most activities that you used to enjoy, even when you do them?
I don’t know if I’d say most. Maybe… some things just feel kind of flat. I still do them, but I’m not really sure what I’m getting out of it.
Looking back, would you say you’ve lost interest in activities you used to care about, even if you still do them occasionally?
I’m not really sure. I guess I still do some of them, so it doesn’t feel like I’ve completely lost interest… but it’s not the same as before.
Can you think of a time recently when something truly made you feel happy or gave you a sense of pleasure, even for a little while?
I’m not sure. Nothing really comes to mind right away… maybe little moments, but I wouldn’t say I felt truly happy.
Would you say that most days, you feel down or sad most of the time, even when there’s no clear reason for it?

Yeah… most days. It’s kind of been like that for a couple years, I guess. Even if I’m at work or church or with people I care about, I still feel low… like heavy or empty, and it doesn’t really go away.
Would you say that most days you feel a depressed mood, such as feeling sad, down, or empty, for most of the day?
Yeah… most days, for most of the day. It’s like this low, empty feeling that’s just there, even when I’m at work or church or with people. It doesn’t really lift.
Have you noticed that you’ve been feeling tired or lacking energy most days, even if you’re not doing much?
Yeah… I feel tired most days. Even little things, like doing inspection logs at work or washing my hair, feel like they take more energy than I have. Resting on my days off doesn’t really help much.
Would you say that you’ve completely lost interest in things you used to care about, even if you still do them sometimes?
I don’t know if I’d say completely. I still do some things… I just don’t really feel much from them, I guess.
Have you noticed any trouble thinking clearly, concentrating, or making decisions lately?
I’m not really sure. I mean… I guess I zone out sometimes, but I haven’t really paid attention to it like that.
Would you say that you’ve experienced a loss of pleasure in most of the activities you used to enjoy, even when you still do them occasionally?
I’m not sure… maybe not “most.” I still do things sometimes, but it’s hard to tell if I’m actually enjoying them or just doing them.
Would you say that most of the things you used to enjoy, like hobbies or time with loved ones, no longer bring you any pleasure, even when you still do them?
I don’t know… I wouldn’t say “no pleasure” exactly. It’s more like I do them and it feels kind of flat, but I’m not sure if that’s most things or just some days.
Would you say that activities you used to enjoy, like hobbies or time with friends, now feel completely unmoving or bring you no pleasure at all, even when you still participate in them?
I don’t think I’d say completely no pleasure. It’s more just… I’m not sure. Sometimes it feels pretty flat, but I don’t know how to measure that.
Would you say that most of the things you used to enjoy, like hobbies or time with loved ones, now bring you little or no pleasure, even when you still do them?
I’m still not totally sure. I guess some things don’t feel like much anymore, but saying most of them bring little or no pleasure feels… I don’t know, hard to say.
Would you say that most of the things you used to enjoy, like hobbies or time with loved ones, now bring you little or no pleasure, even when you still do them?
I’m sorry, I still don’t really know how to answer that. It’s not like I feel nothing, exactly… I just can’t tell if it’s “most things” or not.
Would you say that activities you used to enjoy, like hobbies or time with loved ones, now feel less pleasurable or almost mechanical, even when you still do them?
Maybe… less than before, yeah. I still do things sometimes, but I don’t really know if I’d call it mechanical. It’s just kind of muted, I guess.
Would you say that most of the things you used to enjoy, like hobbies or time with loved ones, now bring you little or no pleasure, even when you still do them?
I don’t really know. I’ve tried to think about it, but “most things” feels too definite. Some stuff feels flatter than it used to, but I can’t say it’s little or no pleasure across the board.

inference_history.note: The patient has endorsed a persistent low mood for most days over the last couple of years, anhedonia (diminished pleasure in previously enjoyable activities), and fatigue. This supports a diagnosis of a depressive disorder. The chronic nature of the symptoms (lasting >2 years) suggests Persistent Depressive Disorder (PDD), which includes the ICD-10 codes F33.1 (moderate), F33.2 (severe), and F34.1 (dysthymia). Major Depressive Disorder (F32.9 or F33.0) is less likely as the symptoms appear chronic rather than episodic. F33.0 was ruled out due to insufficient evidence of a single severe episode, and F32.9 is unlikely due to the duration of symptoms exceeding an acute episode.
